stories.headline: Samsung posts record quarter as memory profit explodes, warns chip shortage runs into 2028

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics reported record Q2 2026 revenue of 171.5 trillion won (about $119B) and operating profit of 89.5 trillion won (about $62B), up 28% and 56% respectively from the prior quarter
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics on Thursday reported a record operating profit of 89.5 trillion won ($62 billion) for the April-June period... Samsung's quarterly revenue of 171.5 trillion won ($119 billion) was also an all-time high.

key_facts.fact: Operating profit was up 1,813.83% year over year, and revenue up 130%, both all-time records
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue rose 130 percent from a year earlier to 171.5 trillion won, while operating profit jumped 1,813.83 percent to 89.5 trillion won.

key_facts.fact: The Device Solutions (chip) division alone produced 127.5 trillion won of revenue and 89.2 trillion won of operating profit — essentially all group profit — with record DRAM and NAND bit sales
key_facts.excerpt: the Device Solutions (DS) division, which oversees the semiconductor business, led overall performance with sales of approximately 127.5 trillion won and operating profit of 89.2 trillion won.

key_facts.fact: Samsung expanded HBM4 supply and became the first in the industry to ship HBM4E samples to major customers; R&D spending hit a record 16 trillion won
key_facts.excerpt: The memory business achieved its largest quarterly performance ever by expanding HBM4 supply and shipping HBM4E samples for the first time in the industry... The R&D cost was 16 trillion won, the highest ever.

key_facts.fact: On the earnings call Samsung said Q3 HBM4 revenue will more than triple quarter on quarter and that HBM4 will comfortably exceed 60% of total HBM revenue in the second half, while the loss-making foundry division is approaching break-even
key_facts.excerpt: "Third-quarter HBM4 revenue will expand more than threefold from the previous quarter," and added, "In the second half, HBM4 revenue will comfortably exceed 60% of total HBM revenue."... a turnaround to profit at the foundry division—which had recorded trillion-won losses every quarter—had grown closer.

key_facts.fact: Memory executive vice-president Kim Jaejune said the gap between chip supply and demand will widen further in 2027 and the shortage is expected to persist into 2028
key_facts.excerpt: Kim Jaejune, an executive vice-president of Samsung's memory chip division, said the company expects the gap between chip supply and demand to widen further in 2027. He said the shortage was expected to persist into 2028.

key_facts.fact: Samsung's results came one day after SK Hynix's own record quarter; the two are the world's largest memory chipmakers
key_facts.excerpt: a day after crosstown rival SK Hynix also reported record earnings, as the world's two largest memory chipmakers continue to ride the global artificial intelligence boom.

stories.headline: Qualcomm warns Apple revenue will fall faster as memory costs squeeze phone chips

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm reported fiscal Q3 revenue of $9.95B, down 4% year over year but above the $9.67B consensus, with non-GAAP EPS of $2.21 versus $2.23 expected
key_facts.excerpt: EPS: $2.21, adjusted, versus $2.23 estimated. Revenue: $9.95 billion versus $9.67 billion estimated

key_facts.fact: Guidance for the current quarter is adjusted EPS of $2.05-$2.25 versus $2.36 expected, on revenue of $9.7B-$10.5B versus $10.02B expected
key_facts.excerpt: Qualcomm expects adjusted profit to be between $2.05 and $2.25 per share in the fourth quarter, below analysts' average estimate of $2.36... It forecast revenue of between $9.7 billion and $10.5 billion during the period, compared with estimates of $10.02 billion.

key_facts.fact: Because of supply constraints, Qualcomm now expects an accelerated step-down in Apple product revenue starting in Q4, with its modem share in the coming iPhone launch 'materially lower' than its earlier 20% estimate
key_facts.excerpt: As a result of our supply constraints, we now expect an acceleration in the step down of Apple product revenues, starting in the fourth fiscal quarter, as our modem share for the upcoming iPhone launch is expected to be materially lower, than our prior estimate of 20%.

key_facts.fact: Handset chip revenue fell 20% to $5.09B; Qualcomm expects Android handset revenue to drop about 20% in fiscal 2026 because of unprecedented memory pricing, cutting annual EPS by more than $1.50
key_facts.excerpt: Unprecedented increases in memory pricing and supply constraints have created significant cyclical headwinds for the global smartphone industry in FY26. As a result, we expect QCT Android Handset revenues to decline by ~20% versus the prior year, driving a reduction in annual EPS by greater than $1.50.

key_facts.fact: CEO Cristiano Amon said non-handset revenue growth, including data center, should accelerate from 24% in fiscal 2026 to more than 60% in fiscal 2027, targeting $40B of non-handset revenue by fiscal 2029; the quarter also closed Qualcomm's acquisition of Modular Inc
key_facts.excerpt: total non-handset revenues growing to $40 billion by fiscal 2029... we expect year-over-year growth in non-handset revenues, including Data Center, to accelerate from 24% in fiscal 2026 to greater than 60% in fiscal 2027... Completed Acquisition of Modular Inc

key_facts.fact: Automotive revenue rose 61% to $1.59B and IoT rose 9% to $1.83B, while total QCT chip revenue fell 5%; shares dropped in extended trading
key_facts.excerpt: QCT revenue was $8.5 billion, including handsets $5.1 billion (down 20%), automotive $1.6 billion (up 61%) and IoT $1.8 billion (up 9%)

key_facts.fact: Amon said consumer preference inside the premium tier is shifting toward cheaper and older phones because of memory price increases
key_facts.excerpt: "Consumer preference within the premium category is changing towards a preference to the lower end of the premium, as well to last year's phone, because of the memory price increases," Amon said.

stories.headline: Arm posts record quarter as data center royalties more than double year over year

key_facts.fact: Arm reported Q1 FYE27 revenue of $1.289B, up 22% year over year and a record, beating the $1.26B FactSet consensus
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue reached $1.29 billion, up 22% year over year, driven by record first-quarter licensing and royalty revenue.

key_facts.fact: Royalty revenue rose 22% to $715M and licensing revenue rose 23% to $574M, with data center royalties more than doubling year over year
key_facts.excerpt: Total revenue for Arm in Q1 FYE27 increased 22% year over year to $1.29 billion... with data center royalties more than doubling year over year and the continued adoption of Arm technology with higher royalty rates per chip, such as Armv9 architecture and Arm Compute Subsystems (CSS).

key_facts.fact: Non-GAAP EPS grew 29% to $0.45, above the top end of guidance; GAAP net income was $270M, or $0.25 a share, versus $130M and $0.12 a year earlier
key_facts.excerpt: The British semiconductor design company reported a profit of $270 million, or 25 cents a share. That compares with a profit of $130 million, or 12 cents a share, a year earlier.

key_facts.fact: Arm guided Q2 revenue to $1.38B plus or minus $50M and adjusted EPS to $0.47 plus or minus $0.04, both above analyst estimates of $1.34B and $0.44
key_facts.excerpt: For the second quarter, the company guided for adjusted earnings in a range of 43 cents to 51 cents a share on revenue between $1.33 billion and $1.43 billion. Analysts currently expect second-quarter earnings of 44 cents a share on revenue of $1.34 billion.

key_facts.fact: On the call, management said cloud AI was again the largest driver of royalty growth, citing Arm-based server chips ramping at all major hyperscalers and Arm technology in nearly all leading DPUs and SmartNICs
key_facts.excerpt: the largest driver of royalty growth was cloud AI. Data center royalty revenue continues to more than double year-on-year... driven by the continued ramp of Arm-based server chips at all the major hyperscalers, alongside increasing deployments of data center networking chips, particularly DPUs and SmartNICs

stories.headline: Intel hands Atom x86 processor technology to RosaicLabs, a startup led by a Lip-Bu Tan co-investor

key_facts.fact: Reuters reported on July 29 that Intel has provided a new startup, RosaicLabs Inc., with access to its Atom processor technology, a rare move for a company that has historically not licensed pieces of its x86 architecture
key_facts.excerpt: Intel has provided access to some of its processor technology to a new startup, according to a source and documents reviewed by Reuters, in a rare move for the U.S. chipmaker... Providing access to Rosaic is a rare move by Intel, which has historically not widely licensed pieces of its x86 architecture or provided Atom tech.

key_facts.fact: Intel aims to ship register-transfer level (RTL) code for the Atom cores to the startup, the form designers use to integrate a processor into a custom chip
key_facts.excerpt: Intel aims to ship register-transfer level (RTL) code for the Atom processor tech to the startup, which designers use to describe chip functions, the source said.

key_facts.fact: RosaicLabs filed its first Delaware incorporation documents in May; a July amended filing names Amarjit Gill as CEO and allows a seed round of about $10 million
key_facts.excerpt: The startup, RosaicLabs Inc., filed its first Delaware incorporation documents in May... The amended document indicates Rosaic can seek a seed funding round of $10 million, according to a Reuters analysis of the amended filing.

key_facts.fact: Gill and Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan are longtime co-investors: Gill helped Tan build the founding team at Rivos, which Meta acquired last year after outbidding Intel, and both made seed investments in Nuvia, later bought by Qualcomm
key_facts.excerpt: Rosaic's CEO is Amarjit Gill... a seasoned venture capital investor and chip industry executive who helped Tan build the founding team at another chip company called Rivos, which Meta acquired last year, outbidding Intel. Tan was chairman of Rivos at the time. Tan and Gill both made seed-stage investments in a third chip startup called Nuvia, which was sold to Qualcomm.

key_facts.fact: Rosaic's founding team includes Rivos veterans, and former Rivos finance chief Amit Parikh signed the incorporation document; Intel declined to comment and the deal's financial terms, permitted markets and technical restrictions are not public
key_facts.excerpt: An amended filing dated July 24 named veteran semiconductor entrepreneur Amarjit Gill as its chief executive... The agreement's financial terms, permitted markets, manufacturing conditions and technical restrictions are not public. Intel has not said which Atom core Rosaic will receive.

key_facts.fact: Atom is Intel's low-power x86 line, designed for modest energy use and little heat — attributes suited to mobile and edge devices
key_facts.excerpt: Intel's Atom technology is designed to operate with modest energy and generate little heat, good attributes for mobile and edge devices.

stories.headline: Innolight slips on debut after $6.8B Hong Kong listing, the city's biggest IPO of the year

key_facts.fact: Zhongji Innolight, a Chinese maker of optical transceivers for AI data centers, raised HK$53.4B ($6.8B) pricing its Hong Kong IPO at HK$980 a share, below the HK$1,010 maximum
key_facts.excerpt: The company raised HK$53.4 billion ($6.8 billion) after pricing its initial public offering at HK$980 per share, below the maximum indicated price of HK$1,010.

key_facts.fact: Shares fell on their July 30 Hong Kong debut — down about 5% early and 7.4% below the issue price at HK$908 by the midday break — amid a global sell-off in AI stocks
key_facts.excerpt: By the midday break, the company's shares had slipped 7.4 per cent below their issue price to trade at HK$908... the listing has coincided with a global sell-off of AI-related stocks

key_facts.fact: The deal was Hong Kong's largest IPO of 2026 and Asia's second largest this year, behind memory maker CXMT's $8.6B Shanghai listing; Innolight's market capitalisation topped HK$1 trillion
key_facts.excerpt: The deal was Asia's second-largest listing this year, behind Chinese memory-chip maker CXMT $8.6 billion Shanghai listing.

key_facts.fact: Retail investors subscribed roughly 16.8 times the Hong Kong tranche and international investors 9.7 times; gross proceeds were HK$53,410 million against net proceeds of HK$52,891 million
key_facts.excerpt: Final Offer Price HK$980.00 | Maximum Offer Price HK$1,010.00 ... Gross proceeds HK$53,410 million ... Net proceeds HK$52,891 million ... Subscription Level 9.73 times

key_facts.fact: Innolight is the world's largest supplier of optical interconnect solutions by revenue, with 21.2% of the global market in 2025, and plans to spend proceeds on R&D, overseas production capacity, supply chain and acquisitions
key_facts.excerpt: the world's largest provider of optical interconnect solutions by revenue, accounting for 21.2% of the global market in 2025, according to consultancy CIC as cited in its prospectus.

key_facts.fact: Days before the debut the company announced an A-share buyback of up to 8 billion yuan ($1.2B); its Shenzhen-listed stock had slumped 16% since the H-share offering launched
key_facts.excerpt: Days ahead of its Hong Kong debut, Innolight announced an A-share buy-back plan worth up to 8 billion yuan (US$1.2 billion)... The company's share price in Shenzhen had slumped 16 per cent since the launch of its H-share public offering as of Wednesday

stories.headline: EU opens bidding for seven AI gigafactories, aiming to mobilise 30 billion euros

key_facts.fact: The European Commission published the long-delayed call for tenders on Thursday, a 5 billion euro EU procurement notice covering a multi-site, multi-country design for seven AI gigafactories
key_facts.excerpt: The EU published a long-awaited call-for-tender to build flagship AI compute infrastructure on Thursday – with a €5 billion EU funding procurement notice covering a multi-site, multi-country design for seven AI gigafactories.

key_facts.fact: Total investment for the seven sites is put at 30 billion euros: 5 billion from the EU, 5 billion from member states and 20 billion from private investors; the call closes on 12 November
key_facts.excerpt: The total investment for seven gigafactories will amount to €30 billion: €5 billion from the EU, €5 billion from EU countries and €20 billion from private investors... The call for tenders is due to close on 12 November.

key_facts.fact: Applicants must show measures to mitigate 'vendor lock-in', a provision aimed at limiting Nvidia's dominance in data center AI chips, with low-scoring consortia facing disqualification
key_facts.excerpt: The call for proposals includes a measure aimed at limiting Nvidia's dominance in AI chips for data centres: Applicants must demonstrate measures applied to mitigate "vendor lock-in", with low-scoring consortia facing disqualification.

key_facts.fact: Funding runs through the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking with 18 member states, in two strands worth up to 500 million euros and up to 1 billion euros per facility; award decisions are expected in early 2027
key_facts.excerpt: Funding is to be channelled through the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU). That body, together with 18 member states including Spain, will jointly buy access to the computing power... The first carries European funding of up to €500 million per facility and the second up to €1 billion... The EC said it expected to take award decisions in early 2027

key_facts.fact: The Commission expanded the plan from four or five sites to up to seven after 76 expressions of interest covering 60 sites in 16 member states; construction is to start in early 2027 and the facilities to be operational by mid-2028
key_facts.excerpt: the Commission has expanded its initial scope from four or five gigafactories to up to seven... The successful projects are expected to begin physical construction of the gigafactories at the start of 2027, with facilities due to become operational by mid-2028.

key_facts.fact: Each gigafactory is to house at least 100,000 cutting-edge AI chips, about four times more powerful than data centers now running in the EU, whose current compute would more than double once the seven sites come online
key_facts.excerpt: Firms can now bid for contracts to build gigafactories that are planned to have at least 100,000 cutting-edge AI chips, making them roughly four times more powerful than the data centres currently running in the EU.

key_facts.fact: The initiative dates to von der Leyen's February 2025 pledge to mobilise 20 billion euros for several gigafactories; the formal tender had been due at the end of 2025 and was twice delayed
key_facts.excerpt: Commission President von der Leyen announced in February 2025 that EUR 20 billion will be mobilised to finance the deployment of several AIGF across the EU... The European High-Performance Computing Joint Undertaking is expected to publish the official call in summer 2026.

stories.headline: Microsoft and Meta lift data center spending again: $41B and $31B of capex in one quarter

key_facts.fact: Microsoft's April-June capital expenditures were $41 billion, up more than 70% year over year, with roughly two-thirds going to short-lived assets — mainly CPUs and GPUs — and $5.6 billion in finance leases
key_facts.excerpt: Capital expenditures were $41 billion in the quarter; roughly two-thirds went toward short-lived assets, primarily CPUs and GPUs, while finance leases totaled $5.6 billion.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft added 88 data centers in fiscal 2026 and another 1 GW of capacity in the fourth quarter, spending nearly $116 billion on property and equipment for the year, with property and equipment rising to $313.1 billion from $205.0 billion
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft accelerated its AI infrastructure expansion in fiscal 2026, adding 88 data centers during the year, another 1 GW of capacity in the fourth quarter, and nearly $116 billion in property and equipment spending... Property and equipment increased to $313.1 billion from $205.0 billion a year earlier

key_facts.fact: Microsoft will now spread long-term data center leases over 25 years instead of 15, lowering reported capex: it guided to about $175 billion for calendar 2026 versus its own prior $190 billion estimate, and more than $50 billion in the current quarter, while saying spending plans are unchanged
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft also said it would now spread long-term leases on data centers over 25 years rather than 15, which has the effect of lowering its annual reported capital expenditures. Microsoft said its spending plans remain unchanged and that it expects reported capital expenditures of $50 billion for the fiscal first quarter of 2027 and $175 billion for the 2026 calendar year.

key_facts.fact: In a securities filing Microsoft disclosed $329.1 billion of data center leases that have not yet commenced, starting between fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2033
key_facts.excerpt: In a securities filing, Microsoft said it has data center leases of $329.1 billion that have not yet commenced, with leases starting between its fiscal year 2027 and fiscal year 2033.

key_facts.fact: Meta spent $31.08 billion on capex including finance leases in the quarter, 83% more than a year earlier, and narrowed its 2026 capex range upward to $130-145 billion from $125-145 billion
key_facts.excerpt: The company recorded $31.08 billion of capital expenditures, including finance lease principal payments, during the three months ended June 30. That was 83% above the $17.01 billion recorded on the same basis a year earlier... narrowing the range to $130 billion to $145 billion

key_facts.fact: The buildout consumed nearly all of Meta's operating cash flow: free cash flow fell to $784 million from $8.55 billion a year earlier, and net property and equipment reached $225.72 billion, up 28% since the end of 2025
key_facts.excerpt: Operating cash flow rose 25% to $31.86 billion, but free cash flow fell to $784 million from $8.55 billion... Net property and equipment reached $225.72 billion at June 30, up $49.32 billion, or 28%, from the end of 2025.

key_facts.fact: Meta confirmed the 2026 capex guidance in its results release and guided Q3 revenue to $61-64 billion
key_facts.excerpt: We anticipate 2026 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, to be in the range of $130-145 billion, narrowed from our prior outlook of $125-145 billion.
